advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Implement (or explicitly document as out-of-scope) the SNAPSHOT.compiled_state fallback so tickets whose CREATE/EDIT were compacted into a snapshot can still reconstruct instead of being force-marked unverified.
evidence: corpus.py:36 `_CONTENT_TYPES = {"CREATE", "EDIT", "FILE_IMPACT", "REVIEW_RESULT"}` — no SNAPSHOT
corpus.py:167-169 `creates = ticket_events.get("CREATE", []); create_found = bool(creates)` — a compacted-away CREATE yields create_found=False -> unverified
ticket 471c-f71f-342c-45ed approach step 2: 'Fall back to the nearest `SNAPSHOT.compiled_state.description` and mark `unverified` when no candidate matches'
mine_outcome_corpus.py:14-19 documents that CREATE/STATUS events are 'folded into a single *-SNAPSHOT.json and their individual event files are deleted with no .retired copy'
advisory.finding: The SNAPSHOT compiled_state fallback specified by the ticket approach is not implemented: compaction folds CREATE/EDIT events into *-SNAPSHOT.json (per the referenced mine_outcome_corpus.py), but _CONTENT_TYPES excludes SNAPSHOT and _reconstruct_material only replays CREATE/EDIT/FILE_IMPACT. A ticket whose CREATE was compacted has create_found=False and is marked unverified rather than reconstructed from the snapshot, silently deflating verified_ratio for older/compacted tickets.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Coerce reconstructed description to str (mirroring mine_outcome_corpus.py's str(...)) so a null/non-str description cannot crash the whole build.
evidence: corpus.py:171 `description = create_data.get("description", "")` — default only applies when the key is ABSENT; an explicit null stays None
corpus.py:182-183 `if "description" in fields: description = fields["description"]` — assigns the raw value with no coercion
material_diff.py:84 `text = description.replace("\r\n", "\n")...` raises AttributeError on None
mine_outcome_corpus.py:294,301 coerce with `str(ce.get("data", {}).get("description", ""))` / `str(fields["description"])` — this new code omits that guard
advisory.finding: description reconstructed from CREATE/EDIT is not coerced to str and can be None (a CREATE/EDIT whose stored description or fields.description is JSON null), which crashes canonical_description->normalize_insignificant_whitespace (`description.replace(...)`), aborting the entire build_corpus run for the whole store.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap with str(...): `description = str(create_data.get("description", "") or "")` and `description = str(fields["description"] or "")` when applying an EDIT.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle/normalize a missing verdict (e.g. bucket under an explicit "MISSING" key or skip) so a null verdict is visible rather than a `null`-keyed histogram bucket.
evidence: corpus.py:317-318 `verdict = row["verdict"]; verdict_histogram[verdict] = verdict_histogram.get(verdict, 0) + 1`
corpus.py:276 `"verdict": data.get("verdict")` — may be None
advisory.finding: verdict_histogram is keyed on data.get("verdict"), which is None when a sidecar lacks a verdict; a None key is serialized into the manifest JSON (as the string key "null"), producing an ambiguous histogram bucket rather than surfacing the malformed sidecar.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the _load_ticket_events and _reconstruct_material docstrings to state that FILE_IMPACT events are also read and replayed.
evidence: corpus.py:131-132 `"""... Only CREATE/EDIT/REVIEW_RESULT content is read."""` but corpus.py:36 `_CONTENT_TYPES` includes FILE_IMPACT and corpus.py:189-194 replays FILE_IMPACT
corpus.py:159 `Replay CREATE + EDITs up to ``review_ts``` — omits FILE_IMPACT despite the loop at 189-194
advisory.finding: Docstrings state only CREATE/EDIT content is read and replayed, but the code now also reads and replays FILE_IMPACT events (the central fix of this change) — the stale docstrings contradict the implementation.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a REVIEW_RESULT whose `reviewed_related_material` includes a child entry and whose fingerprint was signed over a PlanContext with that child, asserting it verifies.
evidence: corpus.py `_child_ids`: `if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("role") == "child" and item.get("canonical_id")`
corpus.py `_build_sidecar_row`: `children = _child_ids(data.get("reviewed_related_material"))` then passed into `_build_context`
Every test fixture uses `"reviewed_related_material": []` — e.g. test_build_corpus_verifies_intact_edit_history, so the child branch is never entered

Concrete violating input: a REVIEW_RESULT with `reviewed_related_material: [{"role": "child", "canonical_id": "0000-0000-0000-00aa"}]` whose fingerprint was signed over a context with that child would exercise the branch and is untested
corpus.py: `_SCHEMAS = {"plan_review_result_v1", "plan_review_result_v2"}`
All fixtures set `"schema": "plan_review_result_v2"`; grep shows no `plan_review_result_v1` in the test file
manifest asserts only `schema_histogram["plan_review_result_v2"]`; `plan_review_result_v1` count is never asserted non-zero
corpus.py: `for e in ticket_events.get("FILE_IMPACT", []): ... file_impact = data.get("file_impact") or []` (LWW replace over all events <= review_ts)
test_build_corpus_reconstructs_declared_file_impact_from_file_impact_events and the 'none' variant each write exactly one FILE_IMPACT event
advisory.finding: The added `_child_ids` logic and children reconstruction in `_build_sidecar_row` (filtering `reviewed_related_material` by `role == "child"` and `canonical_id`, then feeding those ids into the PlanContext used for fingerprint matching) is never exercised by any test — every `review_result` fixture passes `"reviewed_related_material": []`. A regression in child-id extraction (wrong key, dropped role filter) would leave all tests green while causing real sidecars whose signed material included children to silently fail verification.
merged_from: The `plan_review_result_v1` schema branch is claimed as in-scope (`_SCHEMAS = {"plan_review_result_v1", "plan_review_result_v2"}` and reported in `schema_histogram`) but no test exercises a v1 sidecar — every fixture uses `plan_review_result_v2`. The v1 acceptance path (`review_event["data"].get("schema") not in _SCHEMAS`) has no regression coverage.

The FILE_IMPACT last-write-wins replay loop (which reassigns `file_impact`/`scope`/`reason` on every event up to review_ts) is only tested with a single FILE_IMPACT event. A ticket with multiple FILE_IMPACT events where a later one overrides an earlier one (e.g. declaring paths then switching to scope='none') is untested, so a regression in ordering/override would not be caught.
scenarios: A sidecar signed over material that included child tickets
A regression that drops/renames the child role or canonical_id key
